question: For $f(x)=2\sin x+\cos 2x$ on the closed interval $[0,\pi]$, determine all critical points and intervals of increase and decrease, classify the critical points using both derivative tests, and hence find the absolute maximum and minimum values of the function.
explanation:
Critical Points
$$f'(x)=2\cos x-2\sin 2x$$
Using $\sin 2x=2\sin x\cos x$,
$$f'(x)=2\cos x(1-2\sin x)$$
Therefore, $f'(x)=0$ when
$$\cos x=0\quad\text{or}\quad \sin x=\frac{1}{2}$$
In $(0,\pi)$, the critical points are
$$x=\frac{\pi}{6},\quad\frac{\pi}{2},\quad\frac{5\pi}{6}$$

Intervals and First Derivative Test
The derivative is positive on $\left(0,\frac{\pi}{6}\right)$, negative on $\left(\frac{\pi}{6},\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$, positive on $\left(\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{5\pi}{6}\right)$ and negative on $\left(\frac{5\pi}{6},\pi\right)$. Hence, $f$ is increasing on
$$\left(0,\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\cup\left(\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{5\pi}{6}\right)$$
and decreasing on
$$\left(\frac{\pi}{6},\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\cup\left(\frac{5\pi}{6},\pi\right)$$
The first derivative test gives local maxima at $x=\frac{\pi}{6}$ and $x=\frac{5\pi}{6}$, and a local minimum at $x=\frac{\pi}{2}$.

Second Derivative Test
$$f''(x)=-2\sin x-4\cos 2x$$
$$f''\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)=-3<0,\qquad f''\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=2>0$$
$$f''\left(\frac{5\pi}{6}\right)=-3<0$$
This confirms the classification.

Absolute Values
Evaluating the function at the critical points and endpoints,
$$f(0)=1,\quad f\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)=\frac{3}{2},\quad f\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=1$$
$$f\left(\frac{5\pi}{6}\right)=\frac{3}{2},\quad f(\pi)=1$$
Therefore, the absolute maximum value is $\frac{3}{2}$, attained at $x=\frac{\pi}{6}$ and $x=\frac{5\pi}{6}$, while the absolute minimum value is $1$, attained at $x=0$, $x=\frac{\pi}{2}$ and $x=\pi$.

options.A: Critical point $\frac{\pi}{2}$ only; increasing on $\left(0,\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$ and decreasing on $\left(\frac{\pi}{2},\pi\right)$; absolute maximum $1$ and minimum $-1$
options.B: Critical points $\frac{\pi}{3},\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{2\pi}{3}$; decreasing first, increasing next; absolute maximum $2$ and minimum $0$
options.C: Critical points $\frac{\pi}{6},\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{5\pi}{6}$; increasing on $\left(0,\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\cup\left(\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{5\pi}{6}\right)$ and decreasing on the other two subintervals; local maxima at $\frac{\pi}{6},\frac{5\pi}{6}$ and local minimum at $\frac{\pi}{2}$; absolute maximum $\frac{3}{2}$ and absolute minimum $1$
options.D: Critical points $\frac{\pi}{6},\frac{5\pi}{6}$ only; both are local minima; absolute minimum $\frac{3}{2}$ and maximum $1$
